source_gaps: Pages were read with WebFetch, which returns a processed version of each page, so verified_excerpt values are the wording WebFetch returned and were not checked byte for byte against the raw page. The Android page gives airplane mode steps with waits of a set number of seconds and the router restart steps with waits; these durations are left out of the text because replies may not state durations. The iPhone page's reset network settings and ISP notes are not used because they fall outside the three checks in this batch. The iPhone page covers iPhone and iPad; only iPhone steps are used.

source_refs.title: If you can't connect to Wi-Fi on your iPhone or iPad
source_refs.applicability: iPhone; the page says if you still see No Internet Connection, check your router and network settings
source_refs.verified_excerpt: If you can't connect to Wi-Fi, then check your Wi-Fi settings or troubleshoot network issues.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Open the 'Settings' app. Tap 'Wi-Fi' and confirm it's turned on. Tap the name of the network you want to join. Look for a blue checkmark to confirm the connection. If you still can't connect, return to Settings and confirm 'Airplane Mode' is off. Tap 'Wi-Fi' again and check that 'Connectivity Assist' is off. If the Wi-Fi setting is dimmed, restart the device. If you still see 'No Internet Connection,' check your router and network settings.

source_refs.title: Fix internet connection problems on Android devices
source_refs.applicability: Android devices; labels vary by device and the page says so for its general steps
source_refs.verified_excerpt: If you can't access the Internet on your Android device, either through an app or a website, try these troubleshooting steps.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Open Settings, tap 'Network & Internet' or 'Connections', then 'Wi-Fi'. Turn 'Wi-Fi' on. Check the Wi-Fi indicator at the top of the screen. If it isn't shown, or no bars are filled in, you may be out of range. Move closer to the router, confirm you have a stronger signal, and try again. If problems persist, contact your internet service provider or the host of the Wi-Fi network.
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; steps paraphrased from the Fix Wi-Fi problems section; labels kept exactly; the restart-router waits are omitted; straight apostrophes used; excerpt quoted as WebFetch returned it

source_refs.title: Fix internet connection problems on Android devices
source_refs.applicability: Android devices; labels vary by device; if you don't see the mobile data switch, the page says to select Data usage first
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Look for a data indicator, such as 2G, 3G, 4G, or H, next to the signal bars.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Open Settings, tap 'Network & internet' or 'Connections', then 'Mobile data' or 'Cellular data'. If you don't see it, first select 'Data usage'. Turn the switch on. If it's already on, turn it off and back on. Look for a data indicator (2G, 3G, 4G, or H) beside the signal bars at the top of the screen. If Wi-Fi is active, that indicator may not appear, so turn Wi-Fi off and check again. If no data indicator appears, you may be out of coverage. Move somewhere else or go outside and check again. If this happens often, contact your mobile service provider.
